kata.name: Singleton duplicate instance with equal intrinsic values - the value-injectivity key fires on the duplicate pair and the conventional count test names the same element (parity, not cardinality)
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md Singleton row (unexpressible: unique element - object identity has no predicate); fixtures/katas/singleton/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.7
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: the accepted key {Engine:[mode]} collides on the two equal-valued Engine rows and emits one executed key violation; the element (the duplicate) is the one the conventional count assertion also identifies, so unique is empty and the entry is killed. Value-injectivity is not the cardinality law, and the companion entry with distinct modes passes the same key with two rows.

expected.detail: Two Engine rows with the same mode; the accepted key {Engine:[mode]} emits one executed violation with the key witness rows [0,1]. The witness proves a value-tuple collision, not a row count: the same key passes the distinct-mode fixture with two rows.

commands: python3 prototype/singleton_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: this fixture yields singleton:engine-duplicate
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/singleton/equal-duplicate-instance.ct.json --json  # exit 3, 1 violation (key witness)

comparison.conventional_baseline: scripted conventional singleton test: exactly one Engine row (count assertion), accessor identity per client, mode coherence

baseline.artifact: prototype/singleton_baseline.py sha256:ff109499c871f2b8361c809daddac175dcac9b805d8227aa938864e8479f5873 (scripted conventional singleton test; executed before the probe arm)

expressibility_gap.invariant: exactly one row of the declared singleton object: |rows(Engine)| = 1
expressibility_gap.why: the key witness is value-injectivity over the existing rows, not a cardinality claim: the same accepted key passes the distinct-mode instance with two Engine rows (ledger seq 2) and emits nothing there, so no key formulation states `the object has one row`; an empty arrow tuple is refused at parse

discrepancies: This is the only entry in which the kernel names the duplicate, and it does so through an author-declared value key. Parity holds at the element level (both arms name the duplicate), so no unique detection is claimed; the count itself remains unsaid.
procedure: 1. The law was named before any fixture: exact cardinality / unique element, |rows(Engine)| = 1 with every access path resolving to that row (fixtures/katas/singleton/README.md).
2. The conventional arm (prototype/singleton_baseline.py, sha256 above) ran first: exactly-one row, accessor resolution and row identity, and mode coherence, over the frozen fault set.
3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`; the construction probe is the same binary refusing an unparseable document.

4. Witnesses were mapped to the pre-registered element vocabulary; unique = executed probe elements minus baseline-identified elements. A key collision and a row count resolve to the same element (the duplicate); a construction rejection is recorded, never counted.
5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed (parity or null); the cardinality half is recorded in expressibility_gap, never invented as a finding.
6. Verdict: the key witness maps to the same pre-registered element the baseline identifies, so unique is empty and the entry is killed (parity, not a cardinality check).
